{{Quote|Massive statues looked as though they had once supported the roof. Now there was no roof, and the statues broken and lay down on the ground. A large stone eye gave me a hostile stare.|[[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], on the ruins of the Elders|<ref name="E1J:QA">''[[Star Wars Journal: Queen Amidala]]''</ref>}}
The "'''Elders'''" was a name used to describe a [[Species/Legends|species]] of spacefaring [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] that first colonized the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] Territories, several millennia before the [[Grizmallt/Legends|Grizmalltian]] [[Human/Legends|Humans]]. A [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-[[Force-sensitive/Legends|sensitive]] people, the Elders used to build temples and monuments, which were scattered throughout the Nabooian landscape. At least a few similar ruins were also found on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Rori/Legends|Rori]]. Upon their arrival, the Elders clashed with the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]], a race of [[Amphibian/Legends|amphibious]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] native to Naboo.

Both Gungan and [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Human Naboo]] scientists agreed that the end of the Elder civilization may have been the result of the Elders' negligence toward their environment. Others have suggested that the Elders were forced to vacate Naboo after a natural disaster or an invasion. [[Standard century/Legends|Centuries]] after the fall of the Elders, [[Archaeology/Legends|archaeologists]] were divided as to whether the statues were giant representations of the vanished species or monumental portraits of their [[Deity/Legends|gods]]. In the last decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the crumbling remnants of the Elders had become objects of worship to the Gungans, who thought the sculptures depicted their own deities and sought refuge among them in times of trouble.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Elder_statue.jpg|thumb|left|100px|The Elders' statues hint at a humanoid lifeform.]]
The vanished [[Species/Legends|species]] who colonized the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] and passed to posterity under the name of "Elders" were shrouded in mystery. Very little was certain about them, and academic theories pertaining to those beings were mainly based on their architectural relics.<ref name="FF59" /> While some [[Archaeology/Legends|archaeologists]] theorized that the [[Stone/Legends|stone]] colossi the Elders left were icons devoted to their [[Deity/Legends|deities]], others suggest they were indeed a depiction of the Elders themselves. If the latter theory was true, the Elders were very similar to [[Human/Legends|Humans]], with an [[Egg/Legends|egg]]-shaped head, two forward-facing [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], a mildly protruding [[Nose/Legends|nose]] bearing two nostrils, and a [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]] with fleshy lips. Their auricles, if they had any, were concealed by pieces of headgear. Still going by that theory<ref name="IWE1" /> and judging by other remains of their stone statues, the Elders had a torso and [[Limb/Legends|limbs]]<ref name="TPMN">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref> ending in fingers,<ref name="AE">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref> which further implied a fairly [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] body structure.<ref name="AE" />

The eyes of the colossi appeared to be closed, as if the figures they depicted were [[Sleep/Legends|asleep]] or [[Meditation/Legends|meditating]]. Their forehead featured a ring-shaped motif, perhaps a stylized third eye. Based on the meditative stance of the stone heads, the archaeologists deduced that the Elders knew of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]&mdash;a mystical energy field that gave [[Force power/Legends|powers]] to those who could use it<ref name="AGTSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref>&mdash;and considered it sacred.<ref name="FF59" /> The appearance of the Elder statues resemble that of another ancient [[Bendu Statue|idol]] worshipped by the [[Order of Dai Bendu]] in the [[Andobi Mountains/Legends|Andobi Mountains]] of [[Ando Prime/Legends|Ando Prime]].<ref name="SWE1R">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']] {{C|PC version}}</ref> In both cases, the statues portrayed humanoids with closed eyes and thick lips.<ref name="FF59" /><ref name="SWE1R" />

On the Elders' humanoid looks,<ref name="FF59" /> it should be noted that the native [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] remained unfazed when the putative first Human colonists landed on Naboo many [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] after the Elders' departure, which suggest that they had seen Humans before. Millennia later, explorers considered that previous visits to Naboo had indeed existed, although they could find no trace of such landings or any official record at all.<ref name="KORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Society and culture==
The Elders arrived on Naboo from another world, which requires [[Realspace/Legends|space]] travel. That means they had reached [[Technology level|space-level]], which was considered to be the final stage of technological development of any civilization.<ref name="GG6">''[[Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters]]''</ref> A people of builders, the Elders erected many [[temple]]s<ref name="IWE1" /> containing archways, columns, and massive statues that supported the roofs.<ref name="E1J:QA" /> The distribution of those ruins suggested that the Elders lived mainly in [[Swamp/Legends|swampy]] areas.<ref name="IWE1" />

Their colossi typically depicted meditating,<ref name="FF59" /> if somewhat awe-inducing,<ref name="E1J:QA" /> individuals wearing headgears in the shape of a truncated cone.<ref name="FF59" /> Occasionally, some were portrayed clutching weapons and staring vacantly into space.<ref name="TPMN" /> Based on the speculations of scientists,<ref name="FF59" /> the Elders may have been among the first civilizations to have conducted a rudimentary study of the Force,<ref name="FF59" /> before the birth of the [[Je'daii Order]] on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]]<ref name="DotJ1">[[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 1|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm'' 1]]</ref> in [[36,453 BBY]].<ref name="Comic Book Resources">{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/nycc-exclusive-ostrander-and-duursema-unveil-star-wars-dawn-of-the-jedi|text=NYCC EXCLUSIVE: Ostrander and Duursema Unveil "Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi"|date=2011-10-13|archivedate=20200817183352|author=Manning, Shaun}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Rori-space.jpg|thumb|200px|The Elders colonized the planet Naboo and its moon Rori in ancient times.]]
The Elders were not indigenous to Naboo, a planet on the outer edge of the Mid Rim, but they were its first recorded external visitors. They set foot on their new [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] in ancient times, while the planet's initially molten core was slowly cooling down until it became solid.<ref name="FF59" /> It happened, in any event, millennia before a group of Humans<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Grizmallt/Legends|Grizmallt]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> colonized Naboo.<ref name="TEA" /> According to tradition, the Elders engaged in [[Ground warfare/Legends|warfare]] with the indigenous Gungans, a race of amphibious sentients.<ref name="TEA" /> Despite the rivalry, the Elders' civilization flourished on Naboo for nearly two thousands of years. As time went by, they built many temples and statues all around the Nabooian countryside.<ref name="IWE1" /> Judging by the similar monuments and colossi that stood on [[Rori/Legends|Rori]], one of the three [[Moon/Legends|moons]] orbiting Naboo, the Elders also established their presence there.<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

The Elders eventually vacated their adopted homeworld.<ref name="TEA" /> According to several Gungan and Naboo chroniclers, the disappearance of the Elders could be attributed to their greed and blatant disrespect of the planet's ecological harmony.<ref name="IWE1" /> Others theorize that Elders relocated some place else in the galaxy when forced to do so by an undetermined catastrophe, either a a natural disaster or an alien onslaught.<ref name="FF59" /> In the last centuries of the Galactic Republic, all that remained of the Elders were massive heads and limbs of stone scattered across Naboo's surface. The archaeologists, however, disagreed on the interpretation of those artifacts: they were unsure if those effigies were representations of the vanished race themselves or giant portraits of their deities.<ref name="IWE1" />

[[File:Nass_on_Sacred_Place.png|thumb|left|200px|Thousands of years after the Elders' disappearance, the Gungans held their ruins as sacred.]]
In any case, millennia after the Elders' mysterious vanishing, the Gungans used their ruins as places of worship, especially the [[Gungan Sacred Place/Legends|Sacred Place]], an abandoned sanctuary hidden in the foothills of the [[Gallo Mountains/Legends|Gallo Mountains]].<ref name="IWE1" /> When the Gungan city of [[Otoh Sancture]] was [[Destruction of Otoh Sancture|razed]]<ref name="SW:GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref> in [[3000 BBY]],<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' places the [[War of the Gungan tribes|Gungan war]], in which Otoh Sancture was [[Destruction of Otoh Sancture|destroyed]], at this [[Time/Legends|time]].</ref> its leader [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Gallo/Legends|Gallo]] chose to rebuild it in the shadow of a few Elder monuments.<ref name="SW:GB" /> Other such ruins included the [[Gungan Caves]],<ref name="Yoda's Challenge">''[[Star Wars: Yoda's Challenge Activity Center]]''</ref> the [[Lianorm Raceway]] [[Podracing/Legends|Podracing]] course,<ref name="RacerRush">{{SWArchive|url=play/online-games/racer-rush|text=Racer Rush|int=Racer Rush}}</ref> and what became [[Rish Loo/Legends|Rish Loo's]] [[Rish Loo's laboratory/Legends|secret laboratory]] around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]].<ref name="Shadow Warrior">{{TCW|Shadow Warrior}}</ref> Despite having fought them in the past, they also considered the Elders' effigies as depictions of their [[Gud/Legends|guds]]&mdash;a Gungan word for [[Deity/Legends|gods]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|376|Gungan sacred place}}</ref> For example, a certain statue overlooking a waterfall was assimilated to [[Dobbis]],<ref name="PFBTS">''[[Episode I Adventures 11: Pirates from Beyond the Sea]]''</ref> goddess of the rain,<ref name="SWGB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' {{C|French edition}}</ref> and another to [[Big Maxiboss Gurunda]].<ref name="PFBTS" /> When the ten-year-old, homesick Human [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] first saw the Sacred Place, he mistakenly identified such colossal remains as "giant Gungan heads carved out of stone," despite the striking phenotypical differences between the Gungans and the sculptures.<ref name="TPMJA">''[[Star Wars Journal: Anakin Skywalker]]''</ref> On the same occasion, [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], the [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] of the Nabooian Humans, found the Elders' statuary eerie and unnerving.<ref name="E1J:QA" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Stonehead_Tatooine.png|thumb|200px|Early concept art showing a head statue on Tatooine]]
Although the giant stone heads built by the Elders first appeared on Naboo in the [[1999]] movie [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']],<ref name="TPM1">{{Film|I}}</ref> they were originally conceived as part of the [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooinian]] landscape. Early concept art from [[1996]] show an [[Eopie/Legends|eopie]] and its rider walking in the sand of Tatooine with a head statue in the background.<ref name="TPMIG">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref> The Elder heads shown in the movie were crafted in the [[Industrial Light & Magic]] model shop by Concept Sculptor [[Mark Siegel]].<ref name="Snap">{{SWArchive|url=episode-i/fun/snapshot/2000/05/snapshot20000522.html|series=Episode I Snapshot|text=Mark Siegel}}</ref>

Whereas ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'' has the Gungans driving the Elders off of Naboo in [[100 BBY/Legends|100 BBY]],<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> the newer reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' places the end of their civilization in 5,032 BBY.<ref name="TEA" />
